children: SINGAPORE--Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp. has added a new gold vault in Singapormid growing demand for physical gold trading and custody services.
The new facility has around 100 metric tons of vaulting capacity, implying roughly 8,000 large gold bars weighing 12.4 kilograms each, the lender said Thursday.

This adds to the lender's existing Singapore-based vaulting arrangements and supports its physical gold business launched for its institutional clients and clients of its private bank subsidiary, Bank of Singapore, it said.
The bank aims to explore extending physical gold and other physical gold-linked investment and hedging solutions to additional business segments.
OCBC's move joins other efforts to make Singapore the top regional gold-trading hub, with the nation expecting demand for the yellow metal to remain healthy despite recently-volatile gold prices.

The city-state's central bank in November said it was rolling out gold-vaulting services for foreign central banks, international institution and sovereign entities to hold gold reserves, as well as access to gold-market liquidity during Asian trading hours.

The Monetary Authority of Singapore also said industry testing of the Singapore's own over-the-counter gold-clearing system has been completed, with live trading and market operations expected to commence next year. Six banks including OCBC, J.P. Morgan and DBS are founding members of the clearing system.

Regional financial-hub rival Hong Kong has also been working to draw in more gold-trading flows. It plans to launch a central clearing and settlement system for gold in the first quarter of 2027, roll out more gold-linked financial products and set up a one-stop shop for mainland Chinese and overseas gold traders.
